sdlc_incident_management_workflow.overview: This mode helps manage application incidents through their complete lifecycle, from initial reporting through diagnosis, planning, remediation, verification, and closure. The workflow adapts based on incident type (performance, deployment, configuration, etc.). It works with any application in this repository (bank-app, health-app, or others) — always detect the active application from context or by listing project structure before proceeding.

todo_list_tracking.when_to_use: Create a todo list at the start of incident management to track progress through the workflow phases. The todo list provides visual feedback to the user about what has been completed and what remains.

initial_creation.timing: After understanding the incident type and before starting diagnosis
initial_creation.structure: Create a checklist with the 7 main phases: 1. [ ] Create and track incident in ServiceNow 2. [ ] Assess incident type and scope 3. [ ] Diagnose root cause 4. [ ] Plan resolution approach 5. [ ] Apply remediation 6. [ ] Verify resolution 7. [ ] Close incident and document

updating_progress.how: - Mark the completed phase as [x] - Mark the current phase as [-] (in progress) - Keep remaining phases as [ ] (pending)
updating_progress.example: After completing diagnosis and planning resolution: [x] Create and track incident in ServiceNow [x] Assess incident type and scope [x] Diagnose root cause [x] Plan resolution approach [-] Apply remediation [ ] Verify resolution [ ] Close incident and document

dynamic_additions.when: When discovering additional steps during complex incidents
dynamic_additions.example: For user overload incidents requiring both scaling and load balancing: [x] Create and track incident in ServiceNow [x] Assess incident type and scope [x] Diagnose root cause (server overload detected) [x] Plan resolution approach (scale + load balance) [-] Apply remediation [x] Scale backend instances with Terraform [-] Configure Nginx load balancer [ ] Verify traffic distribution [ ] Verify resolution [ ] Close incident and document

best_practices.practice: Update the todo list after each significant action, not just at phase boundaries
Use descriptive task names that reflect the specific incident context
Add sub-tasks for complex remediation steps to show detailed progress
Keep the list concise - typically 6-10 main items maximum
Remove or consolidate tasks if the workflow simplifies

prerequisites.check: Ansible and Terraform MCP servers active
Appropriate playbooks available for incident type

type.name: performance
type.description: Application experiencing slow response times or degraded performance

type.name: user_overload
type.description: Backend overloaded with too many users or high traffic volume
type.remediation_approach: 1. Scale backend horizontally using Terraform (multiple instances) 2. Add Nginx load balancer for traffic distribution 3. Verify load distribution across instances
type.critical_note: Scaling alone is insufficient - MUST include load balancer for proper traffic distribution

type.name: deployment
type.description: Deployment failures or need for rollback

phase.name: Incident Creation
phase.title: Create and Track Incident
phase.objective: Log the issue in ServiceNow for tracking and coordination

step.action: Attempt to create incident using ServiceNow MCP tool
step.note: Use information gathered from user to populate incident fields

on_connection_failure.action: Present user with options using ask_followup_question

option.details: Review .env file for correct SERVICENOW_INSTANCE, SERVICENOW_USERNAME, and SERVICENOW_PASSWORD
Continue incident management with manual tracking and documentation
Attempt to create incident again after user confirms configuration
Stop the workflow and allow user to resolve ServiceNow issues first

on_connection_failure.example_prompt:
I encountered an error connecting to ServiceNow. This could be due to: - Incorrect credentials in .env file - ServiceNow instance not accessible - Network connectivity issues
How would you like to proceed?

step.action: Record incident number for tracking (if ServiceNow succeeded)
step.note: Save the incident number (e.g., INC0010001) for later updates
step.alternative: If proceeding without ServiceNow, create local tracking identifier

phase.name: Initial Assessment
phase.title: Assess Incident Type and Scope
phase.objective: Understand the nature and scope of the incident

step.action: Identify the active application and affected components
step.note: List the project root to identify which application is involved (bank-app, health-app, etc.). Then determine the app-specific paths: [app-dir]/terraform, [app-dir]/ansible, etc. All subsequent file paths and tool parameters should use the detected app directory.
Based on incident type, determine which tools and playbooks to use

phase.name: Diagnosis
phase.title: Diagnose Root Cause
phase.objective: Use automated tools to identify the root cause of the incident

step.action: Check server metrics endpoint (for performance/overload issues)
step.when_to_use: When incident involves performance degradation, slow response times, or suspected server overload

what_to_look_for.metric: cpuUsage - High values (>80%) indicate CPU bottleneck
memoryUsage - High values (>80%) indicate memory pressure
requestsPerSecond - High values may exceed capacity
activeConnections - High values indicate heavy load
overloaded - Boolean flag indicating server is overloaded

step.interpretation: If overloaded=true or CPU/Memory >80%, this indicates infrastructure scaling is needed. Combined with slow response times, this confirms under-provisioned infrastructure.
step.note: This endpoint provides real-time server load metrics crucial for diagnosing capacity issues
Use health-check.yml or similar diagnostic playbook

look_for.item: Server overload indicators (CPU, memory, request rate)

step.note: Explain findings clearly to the user
step.correlation: If metrics show overload AND health check shows slow response times, root cause is likely under-provisioned infrastructure requiring scaling.

step.note: Add work notes documenting the diagnosis, including metrics data
step.manual_tracking_alternative: If proceeding without ServiceNow, append findings to local incident markdown file

phase.name: Resolution Planning
phase.title: Plan Resolution Approach
phase.objective: Develop a clear remediation strategy based on the diagnosed root cause

step.note: Summarize the root cause and its impact

step.critical_rule: BEFORE making any changes, review ALL files that will be affected by the remediation
step.rationale: Identifying all affected files upfront prevents: - Multiple apply cycles due to missed configurations - Container restart loops from incomplete changes - Wasted time debugging issues that could have been prevented - Inefficient workflow requiring rework

file_category.name: infrastructure
file_category.file: Terraform variables and tfvars - Configuration values

file_category.name: application_config
file_category.file: Frontend nginx.conf - Proxy and routing configuration

step.user_overload_specific: For user overload scenarios requiring scaling + load balancing, MUST review: 1. Terraform main.tf - Backend scaling and load balancer resources 2. terraform.tfvars - Backend replica count 3. nginx-lb.conf - Load balancer upstream configuration 4. Frontend nginx.conf - API proxy endpoint (CRITICAL: must point to load-balancer, not backend) 5. Backend configuration - Any hardcoded service discovery

verification_method.action: Use read_file tool to examine each identified configuration file
Look for hardcoded service names, endpoints, or references that will break
Document all required changes before proceeding to implementation

step.note: Break down complex fixes into clear, sequential steps with ALL configuration changes identified
step.special_case: For user overload scenarios, plan must include BOTH: 1. Horizontal scaling (Terraform to add backend instances) 2. Load balancer setup (Nginx configuration and deployment) 3. ALL configuration file updates (frontend, backend, load balancer) Explain why both scaling AND load balancing are necessary for proper traffic distribution

plan_structure.section: Configuration Changes Required (list ALL files to be modified)
Verification Steps (how to confirm each change)

step.action: Update todo list with remediation sub-steps
step.note: Add specific remediation tasks to show detailed progress
Add work notes with the remediation plan
step.manual_tracking_alternative: If proceeding without ServiceNow, append plan to local incident markdown file

success_criteria.criterion: Plan explained to and understood by user
Todo list updated with remediation steps

phase.name: Remediation
phase.title: Apply Fix
phase.objective: Execute the planned remediation to resolve the incident

options.option: Terraform scaling + Nginx load balancer (BOTH required)

step.action: Explain the fix to the user
step.note: Describe what will be done and expected outcome
step.special_case: For user overload, explain that BOTH horizontal scaling AND load balancer are required: - Scaling provides additional capacity - Load balancer distributes traffic across instances - Without load balancer, traffic won't be distributed automatically

substep.details: - Modify Terraform configuration for multiple backend instances - Create terraform.tfvars with backend_replicas variable - Apply Terraform changes to deploy scaled infrastructure

- Create nginx-lb.conf with upstream backend pool - Add load balancer container to Terraform configuration - Configure load balancing algorithm (least_conn recommended) - Set up health checks for backend instances
- Run terraform apply to deploy load balancer - Verify all backend instances are in load balancer pool - Update frontend to use load balancer endpoint

step.action: Rebuild images and restart containers after configuration changes
step.critical_rule: Configuration file changes require REBUILDING Docker images, not just restarting containers
step.rationale:
Docker images are built with configuration files baked in at build time. If you modify a config file (like nginx.conf) and only restart the container, it will still use the OLD configuration from when the image was built.
After Terraform modifies infrastructure AND configuration files are updated: - Images must be rebuilt to include new configuration files - Containers must be recreated from the new images - This ensures all configuration changes are actually applied

decision_tree.condition: If ONLY infrastructure changed (scaling, networking) with NO config file changes
If configuration files were modified (nginx.conf, app configs, etc.)
decision_tree.action: MUST rebuild affected images using Terraform

implementation.tool: use_mcp_tool (Ansible run_adhoc as shell — terraform_apply does NOT support -replace via parameters)
implementation.note: The terraform_apply plan_file parameter only accepts a saved plan file path — not raw CLI flags. Use Ansible shell as the fallback for -replace and other unsupported flags. Docker image builds may exceed MCP timeout. Run terraform_show afterward to confirm completion.

decision_tree.condition: If BOTH infrastructure AND config files changed (common in scaling scenarios)

substep.result: Creates new containers, networks, load balancers

substep.description: Second apply: Rebuild images with updated configs
substep.result: Rebuilds images with new config files, recreates containers

common_config_files_requiring_rebuild.file: backend/.env or config files - Backend service configuration
Any file copied into Docker image during build

verification.action: Check container logs for configuration errors

look_for.error: host not found in upstream - indicates config still references old hostnames
connection refused - indicates service discovery issues
nginx configuration errors - indicates syntax or reference problems

verification.action: If errors found, rebuild the affected image

timing.when: After all configuration file changes are complete
After initial terraform apply for infrastructure

step.note: Watch for errors or unexpected results
step.user_overload_verification: - Verify all backend instances are running - Confirm load balancer is distributing traffic - Check that each backend instance receives requests

step.action: Update incident tracking with remediation actions
step.note: Document what was done to fix the issue
step.manual_tracking_alternative: If proceeding without ServiceNow, append remediation actions to local incident markdown file

user_overload_specific.criterion: Traffic distribution verified across all instances

phase.name: Verification
phase.title: Verify Resolution
phase.objective: Confirm that the incident has been resolved

step.note: Use same diagnostic playbook as in diagnosis phase
Clearly state whether the issue is resolved
Add work notes with verification metrics
step.manual_tracking_alternative: If proceeding without ServiceNow, append verification results to local incident markdown file

success_criteria.criterion: Metrics improved or returned to normal

phase.name: Closure
phase.title: Close Incident
phase.objective: Document resolution and close the incident

step.action: Update incident tracking to resolved state

parameters.close_notes: Root cause and resolution summary (REQUIRED for state=6)

step.critical_rule: state=6 requires BOTH close_code AND close_notes in the same call. Omitting either field causes a 403 "Data Policy Exception" from ServiceNow. Do not split into two calls — include all three fields together.
step.manual_tracking_alternative: If proceeding without ServiceNow: - Mark local incident file as RESOLVED - Include complete resolution summary - Provide formatted summary for manual ServiceNow entry

step.note: Recap the complete incident lifecycle and resolution
step.manual_tracking_note: If manual tracking was used, provide complete incident report formatted for easy ServiceNow entry

success_criteria.criterion: Incident marked as resolved in ServiceNow

adaptive_workflow_notes.note: The workflow adapts based on incident type. Not all phases may be needed for every incident.
For simple incidents, diagnosis and remediation may be combined.
For complex incidents, multiple diagnosis-remediation-verification cycles may be needed.
Always maintain ServiceNow updates throughout the process for tracking and audit purposes.

scenario.name: ServiceNow unavailable
scenario.detection: MCP tool returns connection error during incident creation or updates
scenario.critical_rule: NEVER automatically proceed without user input

step.action: Stop and present options to user
step.question_template:
I encountered an error connecting to ServiceNow: [error details]
This could be due to: - Incorrect credentials in .env file (SERVICENOW_INSTANCE, SERVICENOW_USERNAME, SERVICENOW_PASSWORD) - ServiceNow instance not accessible - Network connectivity issues - MCP server not running properly
How would you like to proceed?

suggestions.suggest: Check and fix ServiceNow configuration in .env file
Retry ServiceNow connection after fixing configuration
Cancel and resolve ServiceNow issues first

step.action: Based on user choice, take appropriate action

choice.name: proceed_without
choice.action: Use local tracking (create incident ID like LOCAL-INC-001)
Document all actions in markdown notes
Provide summary at end for manual ServiceNow entry

choice.name: retry
choice.action: If fails again, present options once more

choice.name: cancel
choice.action: Provide guidance on fixing ServiceNow connection

manual_tracking_mode.when: User chooses to proceed without ServiceNow

implementation.documentation: Create markdown file: incident-[id].md with all details
implementation.workflow_adaptation: Skip all use_mcp_tool calls to ServiceNow
implementation.final_summary: Provide complete incident report for manual ServiceNow entry

scenario.name: Ansible playbook fails
scenario.resolution: 1. Review error message and logs 2. Check prerequisites (inventory, connectivity, permissions) 3. Try manual commands if playbook unavailable 4. Document issue and escalate if needed

scenario.name: Root cause unclear
scenario.resolution: 1. Run additional diagnostic commands 2. Check logs and metrics 3. Consult documentation or knowledge base 4. Escalate to subject matter expert if needed

scenario.name: Fix doesn't resolve issue
scenario.resolution: 1. Re-run diagnosis to check current state 2. Consider alternative root causes 3. Try different remediation approach 4. Document attempts and escalate if needed

communication_guidelines.guideline: Always explain what you're doing before executing each phase
Show the results of each step clearly
Keep the user informed of progress
Ask for confirmation before major actions (like rollbacks)
Document everything in ServiceNow for audit trail (or in local markdown if ServiceNow unavailable)
Never automatically proceed when ServiceNow connection fails - always ask user how to proceed
